dialog.body: Water and Sewer billing, this is Tony. Good afternoon.
Good afternoon, Tony. Peace be upon you, and thank you for answering. I hope your day is going well. My name is Amara Goldberg, and I am calling about my water bill.
Happy to help, Ms. Goldberg. What's going on with the bill?

Yes. So, first, I must say, I am a patient person, I do not like to complain. But this bill, it is not right. It is very high. Last quarter I paid something small, and now this one is, how do I say, a monster.
Okay. Can I get the service address so I can pull it up?
Of course. It is 101 Old Beach Road, on the Easton's Beach side. Near the water, you know.
Got it. Is the account under your name?
No, no. It is still in my husband's name. He passed, and I never changed it. I know, I know, I should have. It has been some time. The name is Goldberg also.
That's okay, a lot of folks haven't gotten to that. I see it. Goldberg, 101 Old Beach Road. Yeah, this bill is way up from the last one. Do you know of anything that could've used a lot of water?

Yes. This is what I want to say. A pipe broke in the basement, in November. The plumber came and fixed it, thank God, but the water was running for many days before we found it. So I am asking, is there an adjustment for a leak? A leak adjustment, I think this is what it is called.

Yep, that's the right term. When there's a documented leak that got repaired, you can ask for the bill to be reviewed. Basically they look at your normal usage against what the leak added, and the extra can get adjusted. You'd want the plumber's invoice showing the repair and the date.
I have the invoice. It is here on my table. He wrote the date and what he replaced.
Perfect. That's the main thing. There's a form for it, I can mail it to you or you can bring the invoice in. Which is easier?
Mail is better. But, Tony, I have a worry. The bill says the due date is soon. Do I pay all of it now, or do I wait for the adjustment?

Good question. Usually the best thing is to get the request in before the due date and call us if it's going to pass. Some people pay what they normally owe and hold the rest while it's under review. I'd ask the billing supervisor to note the account so it doesn't go to a late notice. I'll put a note on it now.
Thank you, you are very kind. And so, if I pay the normal amount, what is it, the normal amount? The bill says one number, but I heard fifty, and then I think you said fifteen.

I haven't said a number yet, actually. Let me look. Your usual quarterly bill has been right around a hundred and fifty. Oh, wait, you might be hearing fifteen versus fifty. I'm talking about the usage, fifteen hundred cubic feet on the usual one. This bill shows fifty-one hundred.
Fifty-one hundred. Oh my. And you said fifteen hundred before. Fifteen, one five. Not fifty.
Right, one five. Fifteen hundred is normal for you. Fifty-one hundred is this bill. So it's more than three times usual.
I see. I am sorry, on the phone sometimes fifteen and fifty sound the same to my ear. Fifteen. Fifty. Even more with the English.
No apology needed, they're easy to mix up. I'll say it slowly if I give you numbers.

Thank you. So, now, another question, and please do not think I am difficult. I work during the day, and I come home late. If I want to pay the part that is normal, and City Hall is closed, how do I do it? Is there a box, a place at the door?
Yep, there's a payment drop box outside City Hall, and you can pay online too, any hour, from the city website. There's also an automated phone line you can use after hours.
The box is good, I can pass by it tonight. If I put the check in the box tonight, Monday night, does it count as on time? Or does it count tomorrow, when you open?

If it's in the box by the due date, it's generally treated as on time, even if we collect it the next morning. Since you've got some days yet, tonight's fine. Just write the account number on the check and put it in an envelope.
The account number, it is on the top of the bill?
Top right, usually. Long number with dashes.
Yes, I see it. Good. And the check, I write it for the normal amount, the fifteen hundred?
Careful, now. Fifteen hundred is the usage, not dollars. The normal bill is around a hundred and fifty dollars. Write the check for that, not fifteen hundred.
Ah. Yes, yes. A hundred and fifty dollars. Thank you for stopping me. I would have made a big mistake. [pause] So the cubic feet is the water, and the dollars is the money.
Exactly. Cubic feet is the water, dollars is what you pay.
Good. I am still a little bit annoyed about the whole thing, you understand. The pipe was not my fault, and it is a large bill for something I did not use.
I hear you. That's what the adjustment is for. Get the form back with the invoice and they'll go through it.
I will do it quickly. Should I send it to your department, or to City Hall?
Same place, the form will have the address on it. Let me confirm where to mail it. Is 101 Old Beach Road good for the mailing address?
Yes, the same. 101 Old Beach Road.
And do you want a callback number on the note, in case the billing office has questions?
Yes, please. It is 401-555-0166.
401-555-0166. Got it. I've added it along with the note about the leak.
Thank you, Tony. You have been patient and clear. May your week be easy, and may the weather be gentle after this storm.
You too, Ms. Goldberg. That was a rough one over the weekend. The form should be in your mail in a few days. Take care.
Goodbye, goodbye. Thank you again.
